name: Marketing, Advertising & Branding

objectives.text: Identify ways a farm or agricultural business tells people about its products
Explain why farmers and agricultural businesses need to market their products to consumers
Describe the four P's of marketing (product, price, place, and promotion) using a local agricultural product as an example
Explain how packaging and labels help promote an agricultural product to shoppers
Distinguish between direct marketing outlets such as farmers markets, roadside stands, and CSAs and commodity marketing through elevators and sale barns
Identify the target market for an agricultural product based on consumer age, location, interests, and buying habits
Compare advertising methods used by agricultural businesses, such as signage, print, radio, and social media
Explain how a brand name, logo, and slogan build customer recognition and loyalty for an agricultural business
Explain marketing principles used in AFNR businesses, including the four P's and the attention, interest, desire, and action model
Define marketing strategies used by AFNR businesses, such as Internet sales, direct to customer sales, and social media promotion
Analyze how market conditions, competition, and price influence the marketing decisions of an agribusiness
Compare and contrast marketing strategies for agricultural products and services, including conventional, commodity, niche, and locally grown markets
Apply branding principles to design a logo and message that represent an agricultural product or SAE enterprise
Summarize the purpose, components, and development process of a marketing plan for an AFNR business
Assess alternative marketing strategies such as value-adding, branding, and niche marketing for an SAE or local agribusiness
Perform a market analysis that examines competitors, customers, and regulations affecting an agricultural product
Develop criteria for evaluating marketing strategies used for agricultural products and services
Evaluate the effectiveness of an existing marketing plan or campaign for an agricultural product or business
Evaluate agricultural advertising claims and label terms such as natural, organic, and locally grown for accuracy and honesty
Develop a complete marketing plan for an agribusiness or SAE enterprise that includes market analysis, branding, advertising, and promotion

changes: Kept all six original objectives, rewording some and aligning the upper-grade ones to AFNR codes. Added foundational objectives for grades 5 to 8: why farms market, packaging as promotion, direct versus commodity marketing, target markets, and how brands build recognition. Added high school objectives tied to specific ABS.05.03 standards: marketing principles including the AIDA model, defining strategies, the market, competition and price context, comparing market types, summarizing marketing plans, assessing alternative strategies, market analysis, and evaluation criteria. Also added an objective on honesty in advertising claims. Sales, product development, and media production were left to the sibling sub-topics.
